# SHIFTS THAT DID NOT COME BACK [color=#7B776F]Pinned. For whole crews. Which shift, how many went, how many came back, and what you were told.[/color]
### #1 papa_of_tomas (OP) // 83.02.02 I posted my son on the wall. I am starting this thread because I have met four other families from the same shift and our stories are not the same story, and they should be.
Chances Claim, deep level, second shift, 83.01.02. Eleven went down. None came up. The mine office told one family it was a gas pocket. It told another it was a collapse. It told a third their man had been moved to a priority project and his letters would be held for security. Same shift. Same lift. Three answers.
### #2 wife_of_aleks // 83.02.03 Port Nereid, north jungle survey. Six went out for three days. The administration said a storm took out their radio and they would walk back. That was two months ago. Nobody walks for two months. The jungle north of the habs is not that big. They sent one search team. The search team came back in half a day and would not say why.
### #3 dam_night_crew // 83.02.09 Raijin hydro, the night maintenance crew on the lower turbines. Seven of them. I was supposed to be on that crew and swapped with a friend so I could go to my daughter's school play. I have not been to a play since.
The official word was a flooding accident. I have worked those turbines nine years. The lower turbine hall floods from the top, slowly, with alarms you can hear in the habs. Nobody heard an alarm. The hall was dry when they let us back in. It had been painted.
### #4 ice_core_relief // 83.02.20 Shivas' Snowball. The relief crew that went out to the ice core labs to take over from the winter team. Five of us went. Three came back, me included, because we were sent home the same day by a security contractor who said the labs were under pest control. The other two were asked to stay because they had lab clearance.
We have never heard from them. When I asked about pest control I was told it was spiders, and the spiders have been on that rock longer than the colony has, and nobody has ever needed a rifle for a spider.
### #5 not_a_shift_boss // 83.03.04 I ran a crew on a mine for six years. I will tell you something about mines that you will not like. When the office tells three families three different stories, it is because nobody in the office knows what happened either. They have been handed a number and told to make it go away. The stories are what they make up on the spot.
### #6 papa_of_tomas (OP) // 83.03.04 Then somebody above the office knows. And the lift shaft is welded shut, so whoever knows does not want it opened.
### #7 porch_light (mod) // 83.03.05 A note on how to compare. Ask the office in writing for the shift roster, the incident report number, and the name of the medical officer who signed the death or transfer notices. Families on the same shift should send the same letter on the same day. When the answers come back different, you have something to show.
Gone Quiet keeps a list of stations that went silent all at once. A shift is a station going silent one lift at a time. Some of yours are on [netlink="their list" link="missing.deep/silent"] already.
### #8 union_widow // 83.05.08 My husband was a shift steward at a mine I will not name, because they still employ my daughter. He kept a book of every shift that came up short. Not the big losses. One man here, two there, over eight years. When he died, the company sent someone to collect his work things before the funeral. They took the book.
He was careful. He made a copy. It is in my kitchen, and it has three hundred and twelve lines in it, and the last line is in his writing and it is the date of his last shift.
I am going to copy one page here each week.
